findings.title: reg_ids accepts an explicit seq: out-of-order gap fill, CAT-000 and negative ids (CAT--03) are minted and the gate reports GATE OK
findings.evidence: Scratch DB from apply_ext.sh; INSERT reg_ids(seq,..) with seq=9, then 5, 0, -3: all accepted (rc=0); rows CAT--03, CAT-000, CAT-005 (minted after CAT-009). gate.sh on that DB: GATE OK. reg_ids_no_replace only refuses an EXISTING seq (register_ext.sql:33-36); no trigger requires NEW.seq IS NULL or NEW.seq > max(seq) or seq >= 1. CAT--03 does not match the engine heading grammar [A-Z]{3}-[0-9A-Za-z]+ (constitution 2026-10-08 extension: malformed keys are dropped by the db->md->db round trip).
findings.violates: 11.4.54 monotonic, no gaps, never renumbered; 11.4.241 (enforce at the strongest rung available: a trigger is available)
findings.fix: BEFORE INSERT ON reg_ids trigger refusing NEW.seq IS NOT NULL (or NEW.seq < 1 or NEW.seq <= IFNULL(max(seq),0)); RED test with the four inserts above; paired mutation.

findings.title: replay.sh reads absent journal fields as their safe value: the round-1 'row dropped/replayed blind with an OK verdict' class has surviving members
findings.evidence: Extracted the verbatim logic of replay.sh and ran it: control needle ids_snapshot='failed' -> refused; same row with the field ABSENT -> accepted ('ok' default at replay.sh:133). changed() (replay.sh:114-115) on a register row with no db_sha_before/db_sha_after/ids_minted/wal fields returns False, so the row is skipped as no_database_change with an OK verdict; control (hashes differ) -> True. Also r.get('db', REGDB) and the optional 'seq' order check (replay.sh:80) default open; base-row 'not r.get("wal_bytes_after")' reads absent as 0.
findings.violates: 11.4.146(D3)/11.4.271 absent-field-is-refused pattern; 11.4.252 fail-closed; 11.4.276(C) class-exhaustive closure of class C1
findings.fix: validate every row against a required-field schema (seq, mode, db, db_sha_before, db_sha_after, ids_minted, ids_snapshot, wal_bytes_before, wal_bytes_after, exit, argv) and REFUSE journal_row_incomplete; tests: one row per missing field must refuse.

findings.title: No DB-level idempotency guard on the id mint (11.4.253); orphan ids are invisible to the gate
findings.evidence: Two identical INSERT reg_ids(minted_by,mint_basis) with mint_basis='import' both succeed (no UNIQUE on minted_by); gate.sh on that DB: GATE OK (no view flags a reg_ids row with no items/reg_source_map row). The importers dedup by check-then-insert on minted_by (import_plan.py:145-149, import_tickets.py:343-348), anti-pattern (i) of 11.4.253; the single-writer lock removes the race but not a retry after an exit-22/unknown-status write.
findings.fix: partial UNIQUE INDEX on reg_ids(minted_by) WHERE mint_basis='import' (or an explicit idempotency_key column); a view_empty check for minted ids with no item after the import completes.

findings.title: ID prefix: CAT is declared in three unconnected places; do not rename atm_id to cat_id
findings.evidence: .helix/reporting.yaml:20 id_prefix: CAT (the declared DATA per the constitution 2026-10-08 extension of 11.4.54/11.4.248); register_ext.sql:23 hard-codes 'CAT-' in the generated column; import_plan.py:162 and import_tickets.py:361 hard-code --prefix CAT. No gate asserts they agree. The constitution states the legacy name atm_id is KEPT (rename to ticket_id is owed ENGINE work needing a schema migration + compatibility view); a local atm_id->cat_id rename would diverge from the engine's own items.atm_id and is not recommended. CAT is uppercase 3 letters, so it is inside the measured safe key grammar.
findings.fix: gate.sh (or apply_ext.sh) compares the DDL literal with reporting.yaml id_prefix and FAILs on mismatch; importers read the prefix from the same file; record in docs/04 that atm_id stays until the engine rename lands.

findings.title: Reviewer mutant MY3 survives test_gate: re-hash of a tracker_receipt that cites a FILE can be skipped
findings.evidence: gate.sh line 153 mutated to '[ "$kind" = tracker_receipt ] && continue; n=$((n+1))'; test_gate.sh with GATE=<mutant>: RESULT pass=126 fail=0. No fixture holds a file-path tracker_receipt whose bytes changed, so a forged receipt (the evidence behind tracker SYNCED) is unguarded against this regression.

findings.title: replay.sh removes an --out directory it did not create
findings.evidence: replay.sh:94-95 sets created=True even when OUT already existed (empty); refuse() then shutil.rmtree(OUT). A pre-existing empty directory, or content written into it by another process after the listdir check, is deleted on any refusal (section 9 data safety).
findings.fix: created=True only when os.makedirs created the directory (or require OUT to be absent); rmtree only paths this run created.

findings.title: locked.sh --out runs skip the orphan-writer fence
findings.evidence: locked.sh: 'if [ "$MODE" != out ] && [ "$NESTED" = 0 ]; then fence_orphans; fi'. A read through --out (replay id reads, export/dump out-mode) can start while a SIGKILLed predecessor's container still writes. SQLite read snapshots keep a single query consistent, so the practical risk is low; documenting the exception (or fencing) closes it.
findings.fix: fence in --out mode too, or document why a concurrent orphan writer is harmless for every --out caller.
